description:
🚀 SURVORA is a multidisciplinary team participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We're building an interactive Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer that combines space science, AI, game development, and creative design to make lunar and Martian survival exciting and educational.

We're looking for passionate people interested in Game Development, AI/ML, Software Engineering, UI/UX, 3D Design, Astronomy, and Physics

No need to be an expert — creativity, commitment, and teamwork matter most
summary:
**SURVORA** is an interactive educational space survival game designed to transform complex space engineering concepts into engaging, hands-on experiences for young learners.

Developed for NASA's **Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer** challenge, SURVORA places players in command of a Martian outpost, where they must manage critical resources such as oxygen, power, water, and food while protecting their crew from environmental hazards.

Unlike traditional STEM learning tools, SURVORA introduces realistic engineering trade-offs through interactive missions. Players face challenges such as oxygen shortages, power failures, and Martian dust storms, where every decision affects the colony's survival.

The game combines strategic base management with third-person exploration, mission-based progression, and **NOVA**, an AI-powered educational companion that provides contextual guidance and scientific explanations grounded in NASA research and data.

By integrating NASA scientific resources into an accessible simulation, SURVORA bridges the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical decision-making.

**Our mission is to inspire the next generation of space explorers by making science something students don't just study, but experience.**
details:
SURVORA — Project Details

What We Developed

SURVORA is an interactive 3D educational survival and exploration game developed for NASA's Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge. Designed for students aged 7–12, it transforms complex space engineering concepts into engaging, hands-on learning experiences.

Players become commanders of a Martian outpost, responsible for managing critical systems such as oxygen generation, electricity, water recycling, food production, and crew safety. Through interactive missions, they face challenges including oxygen shortages, power failures, Martian dust storms, and environmental hazards.

How It Works

SURVORA combines two interconnected gameplay experiences:

Mars Base Management: Players build and manage their colony, allocate limited resources, and make engineering decisions that directly affect mission survival. For example, when oxygen production decreases due to insufficient power, players must decide whether to redirect electricity from research facilities to life-support systems.

Exploration and Missions: Players explore the Martian environment through third-person gameplay, investigate scientific locations, interact with equipment, collect samples, and complete missions to earn Knowledge Points and unlock upgrades.

Every mission follows a learning cycle: Observe → Analyze → Decide → Experience the Consequences → Learn.

AI-Powered Learning with NOVA

One of SURVORA's key innovations is NOVA, an AI-powered educational companion integrated into the learning experience.

NOVA uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to combine the player's current game context with scientific information from NASA and other space-agency resources.

Instead of simply giving answers, NOVA provides contextual explanations, progressive hints, and scientific references that help players understand why their decisions succeed or fail.

The AI provides guidance, while the Unity simulation remains responsible for resource calculations and gameplay outcomes.

NASA Data and Scientific Integration

SURVORA incorporates scientific knowledge from NASA's Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS), MOXIE Mars oxygen-production experiment, Mars exploration research, and space-weather resources such as NASA DONKI.

These resources inform educational explanations and mission scenarios involving life support, solar energy, radiation awareness, and planetary exploration.

We distinguish real scientific observations from simplified gameplay simulations to maintain scientific accuracy while keeping the experience accessible to younger students.

Technologies Used

  • Game Development: Unity 3D and C#.
  • AI Backend: Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, and Google Gemini.
  • Retrieval-Augmented Generation: BM25, ChromaDB, and Sentence Transformers.
  • Scientific Data: NASA research publications, documented scientific datasets, and curated knowledge resources.
  • 3D Development: Low-poly 3D environments, Martian colony structures, exploration assets, and interactive interfaces.

Creativity, Benefits, and Impact

SURVORA's innovation lies in combining strategic resource management, third-person exploration, and context-aware AI guidance within a single educational experience.

Rather than teaching space science through passive explanations, SURVORA allows students to experience engineering trade-offs firsthand. Every decision has consequences, encouraging critical thinking, problem-solving, systems thinking, and scientific curiosity.

Throughout development, our team prioritized scientific credibility, age-appropriate gameplay, accessibility, engaging visual design, and meaningful connections between player choices and educational outcomes.

Our goal is to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and space explorers by making space education interactive, accessible, and exciting.

With SURVORA, students don't just learn how a space mission works — they experience what it takes to keep one alive.
